Setting: Privileged Access Protection In Place (Compliant Device Or Phishing-Resistant Auth Strength For Admins)
Recommendation: Ensure at least one hardening control protects privileged role sign-ins: require a compliant device, or require a phishing-resistant authentication strength for admin roles via Conditional Access. A Privileged Access Workstation (PAW) model or equivalent out-of-band control also satisfies this intent even though it isn't visible to this assessment - treat this finding as a starting point for that conversation, not a mandate for one specific implementation. Operational trap if the compliant-device path is chosen: a Conditional Access policy requiring device compliance or an App Protection Policy can inadvertently block passkey registration itself in the Authenticator app, before an admin has anything to sign in with. Multiple independent practitioner reports converge on excluding three Microsoft first-party service principals from that policy - Azure Credential Configuration Endpoint Service (App ID ea890292-c8c8-4433-b5ea-b09d0668e1a6), Microsoft App Access Panel, and AAD Reporting - none of which Microsoft documents publicly as of this writing. Diagnose via sign-in logs filtered for failed registration attempts citing compliance or App Protection Policy requirements before assuming a stalled passkey rollout for admins is a user-behavior problem.
